summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, chronic diastolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and prior DVT/PE was admitted with cough, low-grade fever, and generalized weakness. She had stopped taking warfarin and furosemide at home, and recently reduced her steroid dose. Evaluation revealed no bacterial infection; symptoms were attributed to a viral syndrome with mild acute on chronic heart failure, which improved with a single IV lasix dose and resumption of oral diuretic. A contaminated urine culture with E. coli was treated with a short course of cefpodoxime. Warfarin was restarted using fondaparinux as a bridge due to poor IV access and failed PICC placement. INR reached therapeutic levels by discharge. CellCept was initiated for polymyositis with a planned titration schedule and weekly lab monitoring. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved strength, and clear discharge instructions for medication management and follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Escherichia coli [E. coli] infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
